items.title: Log helper passes a method object instead of the scrollbar maximum, breaking log output and Apply/Install

findings.title: Log helper passes a method object instead of the scrollbar maximum, breaking log output and Apply/Install
findings.evidence: textEdit.verticalScrollBar().setValue(textEdit.verticalScrollBar().maximum)
findings.explanation: moveTextEditToEnd uses `.maximum` without calling it. onProgressInfo calls this helper on every message, and onApply and onInstall call onProgressInfo before any inference. In PythonQt the `maximum` attribute is a callable, so setValue receives a non-integer and raises. The user would see the Apply or Install action fail before segmentation starts. I could not run this, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestion: Use `textEdit.verticalScrollBar().maximum()` (call the method), and verify on a Slicer build that Apply reaches inference.

items.title: Multi-minute inference runs on the GUI thread without progress or cancel

findings.title: Multi-minute inference runs on the GUI thread without progress or cancel
findings.evidence:
try:
                with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tempDirPath:
                    inputFileName = "volume.nii.gz"
                    inputFilePath = Path(tempDirPath) / inputFileName
                    slicer.util.saveNode(inputVolume, str(inputFilePath))
findings.explanation: onApply calls applySegmentation synchronously from the button slot; the slice loop in PKDIA.py:53-85 never calls processEvents, so Slicer's UI is frozen for the whole run (README says "several minutes"). Users cannot cancel, and the window may be reported as unresponsive. Additionally only RuntimeError is caught (line 156), so an OSError from nibabel or a torch error propagates and leaves all buttons disabled because _setButtonsEnabled(True) at line 158 is never reached.
findings.suggestion: Run the inference in a worker thread (slicer.util.createProgressDialog / qSlicerCoreApplication or a QThread with progress callbacks), and use try/finally to re-enable the UI for any exception.

findings.title: No license or redistribution terms for the downloaded model weights
findings.evidence: ModalityEnum.T2: "https://github.com/conze/SlicerPolycysticKidneySeg/releases/download/v.1.1.0/PKDIAv1-weights.pth"
findings.explanation: The extension downloads PKDIAv1/v2 weights from GitHub releases and provides no license for them. Its acknowledgements say the models were trained on Genkyst cohort data, which may carry its own data-use terms. Users and redistributors cannot tell what they may do with the weights.
findings.suggestion: Add a license or terms-of-use statement for the weights (and any data restrictions) in the repository and release notes.

items.title: Unconfirmed pip installs of Slicer-bundled packages (numpy, scikit-image)

findings.title: Unconfirmed pip installs of Slicer-bundled packages (numpy, scikit-image)
findings.explanation: `pip_install("numpy")` installs a Slicer-bundled package directly, and `pip_install("scikit-image")` resolves numpy/scipy/pillow requirements that pip may upgrade in place. Slicer's own modules and other extensions are compiled against the bundled numpy/scipy, so an upgrade can break them for the whole installation. No confirmation dialog is shown for these installs (doAskConfirmation is only used for PyTorch), and pip_install swallows CalledProcessError and still returns True (lines 169-177), so a failed install is reported as success.
findings.suggestion: Do not install numpy at all (Slicer always ships it); install scikit-image/nibabel with version constraints compatible with Slicer's bundled numpy/scipy, ask the user for confirmation before modifying the environment, and propagate pip failures so the UI reports them.

findings.title: Unpinned pip installs of core packages into the shared Slicer environment
findings.explanation: numpy, scikit-image, nibabel and timm are installed with plain pip install (no constraints), and this happens on a button press or during the self-test. Installing scikit-image can pull or upgrade numpy/scipy that Slicer and other extensions depend on. Users are not asked to confirm these installs, unlike PyTorch.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before installing packages, pin compatible versions, or use constraints that protect Slicer's bundled numpy and scipy.

items.title: pip_install("timm") pulls torchvision from PyPI outside PyTorchUtils

findings.title: pip_install("timm") pulls torchvision from PyPI outside PyTorchUtils
findings.explanation: timm declares torchvision (and torch) as hard requirements. When the user presses "Install dependencies", `slicer.util.pip_install("timm")` resolves torchvision from PyPI, which is not the build installed by the PyTorch extension/PyTorchUtils. A CPU-only or CUDA-mismatched torchvision can break the torch install that PyTorchUtils just set up, affecting every other extension using PyTorch in the same Slicer installation. The policy explicitly requires PyTorch-family packages to come through PyTorchUtils.
findings.suggestion: Install timm with `--no-deps` after ensuring torch/torchvision are provided by PyTorchUtils (e.g. `torchLogic.installTorch(...)` plus a torchvision install through PyTorchUtils), or vendor the small amount of timm functionality used (create_model for swinv2_cr_tiny_ns_224) so no extra dependency is needed.

items.title: pretrained=True triggers a silent HuggingFace download during every Apply

findings.title: pretrained=True triggers a silent HuggingFace download during every Apply
findings.evidence:
net = swinv2Unet.SwinV2TwoDecoder(
        model_name="swinv2_cr_tiny_ns_224",
        pretrained=True,
findings.explanation: timm.create_model(..., pretrained=True) downloads ImageNet encoder weights from the HuggingFace hub the first time (and re-checks the hub on later runs). This happens inside the segmentation call, with no user opt-in and no mention in the README, and it makes Apply fail on offline/air-gapped machines even though the local PKDIA checkpoint is loaded immediately afterwards at line 40 and overwrites those weights. It also adds an unannounced third-party network destination to the module's behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Pass pretrained=False (the state dict is loaded right after) or, if the pretrained encoder is genuinely needed, download it explicitly through the existing "Download weights" flow with a checksum and document it.

findings.title: Pretrained ImageNet encoder is fetched at inference time
findings.evidence:
pretrained=True,
        img_size=(img_size, img_size),
findings.explanation: applyPKDIA builds the network with pretrained=True, so timm may download encoder weights on first use. This is an undisclosed network access, though the trained weights are then loaded over them. It is not clearly documented to users.
findings.suggestion: Use pretrained=False because the trained state dict is loaded anyway, which avoids an extra download.

items.title: Integration test imports submodules as classes and will fail

findings.title: Integration test imports submodules as classes and will fail
findings.evidence: from SlicerPKDIALib import InstallLogic, SegmentationLogic, Widget
findings.explanation: SlicerPKDIALib/__init__.py is empty, so `from SlicerPKDIALib import InstallLogic, SegmentationLogic, Widget` yields module objects. Calling `InstallLogic()` or `SegmentationLogic()` then raises TypeError. The test therefore cannot validate the pipeline, and the only test is also marked slow.
findings.suggestion: Import the classes from their modules, e.g. `from SlicerPKDIALib.InstallLogic import InstallLogic`, and check the test runs in CI.

items.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity verification

findings.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity verification
findings.explanation: The .pth checkpoints are fetched from GitHub releases and loaded with torch.load (PKDIA.py:40). weights_only=True limits pickle-based code execution, but a corrupted or substituted download is still loaded without any SHA256 check, unlike the sample data in PolycysticKidneySeg.py:57/68 which do declare checksums. A truncated download also produces a confusing load error rather than a clear message.
findings.suggestion: Add SHA256 checksums for PKDIAv1-weights.pth and PKDIAv2-weights.pth and verify after download, as already done for the sample volumes.

findings.title: Partial weight downloads are accepted as valid and there is no checksum
findings.explanation: urlretrieve writes directly to the final weights path. A failed or interrupted download can leave a truncated .pth file. areWeightsFound only checks existence, so later torch.load fails with a confusing error. The downloads also have no SHA256 check, unlike the sample data.
findings.suggestion: Download to a temporary file, verify a SHA256 checksum, then rename. Remove partial files on failure.

items.title: No clinical-use disclaimer or validation statement for a medical segmentation tool

findings.title: No clinical-use disclaimer or validation statement for a medical segmentation tool
findings.evidence: This extension allows the use of PKDIA neural networks in 3DSlicer.
findings.explanation: The module produces kidney segmentations used for ADPKD assessment, yet the help text and README have no statement that results are not for clinical decisions, and no validation or intended-use limits are given beyond a citation.
findings.suggestion: Add a research-use-only disclaimer and the validation scope to the help text and README.

items.title: No stated license or terms for the downloaded model weights; no clinical disclaimer

findings.title: No stated license or terms for the downloaded model weights; no clinical disclaimer
findings.evidence: Models were developed and trained by Pierre-Henri Conze (IMT Atlantique) using imaging data from the Genkyst cohort.
findings.explanation: The repository LICENSE is Apache-2.0 for the code, but the PKDIAv1/v2 checkpoints distributed via GitHub releases and the Genkyst cohort data behind them have no explicit license or usage terms, and neither README.md nor the module helpText states that the output is for research use and not for clinical decision making. Users cannot tell what they may do with the weights.
findings.suggestion: State the license/terms of the model weights explicitly (e.g. in README and next to the release assets) and add a research-use-only disclaimer to README and helpText.

items.title: Segmentation geometry may not match the input volume orientation

findings.title: Segmentation geometry may not match the input volume orientation
findings.evidence:
segmentationNode = self.logic.applySegmentation(str(inputFilePath), tempDirPath, modality)
                    segmentationNode.SetReferenceImageGeometryParameterFromVolumeNode(inputVolume)
findings.explanation: The pipeline reorients the volume with nibabel.as_closest_canonical (exam_genkyst_prod.py:23) and writes predictions in that canonical space, while the segmentation node is then given the original volume's geometry. If the loaded volume is not already in closest-canonical orientation, the resulting segments can be displayed misaligned with the image. SetReferenceImageGeometryParameterFromVolumeNode only sets the reference-geometry parameter, not the segment geometry.
findings.suggestion: Either skip as_closest_canonical and work in the volume's own orientation, or resample the prediction back to the input volume geometry before creating the segmentation node.

findings.title: Only RuntimeError is handled in onApply; other failures leave the UI disabled
findings.explanation: onApply disables the buttons, then catches only RuntimeError. A nibabel, timm or shape error inside applySegmentation propagates and the buttons are never re-enabled, so the user must restart the module. Errors are not reported in the log either.
findings.suggestion: Use try/finally to re-enable buttons and report any Exception to the user.

items.title: Validation errors overwrite each other; only the last is shown

findings.title: Validation errors overwrite each other; only the last is shown
findings.explanation: Each failed check replaces errorMessage, so a user with no volume selected and missing weights only sees the weights message and may not understand why Apply does nothing useful. Also areWeightsFound() (SegmentationLogic.py:19-23) requires both T2 and CT checkpoints, so a user who only downloaded one modality is blocked from using it.
findings.suggestion: Collect all failures into a list and display them together; check only the weights file for the selected modality.

items.title: Weights are written inside the extension installation directory

findings.title: Weights are written inside the extension installation directory
findings.evidence:
fileDir = Path(__file__).parent
        self.weightsDir = fileDir.parent / "weights"
findings.explanation: Downloaded checkpoints land in <extension>/weights, i.e. inside the Slicer installation tree. On read-only or system-wide installs the mkdir/urlretrieve fails, and the files are not removed on uninstall. Slicer convention is to store such data in the user's settings/temporary directory.
findings.suggestion: Store weights under slicer.util.settingsValue / a user-writable cache directory (e.g. slicer.mrmlScene temp dir or QStandardPaths AppDataLocation).

items.title: Integration test uses MRHead and an undeclared test-runner extension

findings.title: Integration test uses MRHead and an undeclared test-runner extension
findings.evidence:
SampleData.SampleDataLogic().downloadMRHead()
        widget.ui.modalityComboBox.setCurrentIndex(0)  # T2

        widget.ui.applyButton.click()
findings.explanation: The only integration test feeds a head MR into a kidney model, so it can only assert that two segments were created, not that the pipeline is correct; it is also marked slow and excluded by the module's own `-m not slow` filter. PolycysticKidneySeg.py:93-100 additionally requires the SlicerPythonTestRunner extension, which is not declared anywhere.
findings.suggestion: Use the registered T2/CT sample data in the test and declare SlicerPythonTestRunner as a test dependency in the documentation.
